1.title: AI/ML and Analytics Services
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: A I, M L and Analytics Services, that is, artificial intelligence, machine learning and analytics. This module covers task statement three point seven. You will learn which A W S service understands text, speech and images, which one lets you build your own machine learning models, and which services collect, prepare, analyze and display data. The exam gives you a short description of a need and asks you to name the service.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Match the A I services to the task: text, speech, images, documents and conversation. Say what Amazon SageMaker A I is for, and place Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Q. Describe the analytics flow: Kinesis, Glue, Athena, Redshift, E M R, OpenSearch and Amazon Quick. And choose the right service from a short description of the need.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater Has Data to Use
1.text: Tidewater has data to use. It has thousands of reviews, scanned supplier invoices and recorded support calls. It wants a chatbot for order questions, and product photos checked for unsafe content. Sales files in S three need quick S Q L answers, and the shop's clicks arrive as a live stream. Managers want dashboards, and the data team wants to train its own model. Your job is to choose the A I, M L and analytics services.

1.title: Task First, Then the Service
1.text: For A I services, think task first, then service. Pre-built A I services do one task through an A P I, and you need no machine learning expertise. For text, there are Amazon Comprehend and Amazon Translate. For speech, there are Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Polly. For images, video and documents, there are Amazon Rekognition and Amazon Textract. For conversation, there is Amazon Lex. And if you want to build your own models, there is Amazon SageMaker A I. The figure shows the five groups. Exam tip: name the input, text, speech, image, document or conversation, and the task.

1.title: Text and Documents: Comprehend, Translate and Textract
1.text: Three services work with text and documents. Amazon Comprehend uses natural language processing to find entities, key phrases, sentiment, language and personally identifiable information in text, and it supports custom classification. Ask yourself, what do customers feel? Amazon Translate is text translation with machine learning, used to build multilingual applications. Just translate it. Amazon Textract detects typed and handwritten text and extracts forms and tables, with operations for invoices, receipts and I Ds. Think of reading the scanned form. Exam tip: sentiment in text means Comprehend; text from scanned forms means Textract; translation means Translate.

1.title: Speech, Images and Chat: Transcribe, Polly, Rekognition and Lex
1.text: Four more services cover speech, images and conversation. Amazon Transcribe is speech to text. It converts audio to text, either streaming or in batch from S three. Think of calls to text. Amazon Polly is the opposite, text to speech, with lifelike speech in many languages and voices. Think of reading it aloud. Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video. It detects objects, text, faces and unsafe content, and it compares faces. Think of what is in the picture. Amazon Lex builds chatbots for voice and text, with speech recognition and language understanding. Exam tip: speech to text is Transcribe, text to speech is Polly, pictures are Rekognition, and chatbots are Lex.

1.title: Build Your Own and Ask for Help: SageMaker AI, Bedrock and Amazon Q
1.text: When pre-built services are not enough, you build your own. Amazon SageMaker A I is a fully managed machine learning service where data scientists and developers build, train and deploy their own models. On the third of December, twenty twenty-four, Amazon SageMaker was renamed SageMaker A I, and the name Amazon SageMaker now covers a wider data, analytics and A I platform, so older material may use the old name. Amazon Bedrock gives managed access to foundation models through one A P I, for generative A I applications, though it is beyond the exam guide. Amazon Q Developer is a generative A I assistant that helps you understand, build and operate A W S applications. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, Amazon Q Business is closed to new customers, and A W S points to Amazon Quick, and Q Developer I D E plugins end on the thirtieth of April, twenty twenty-seven. Exam tip: building and training your own models means SageMaker A I.

1.title: From Data to Decisions: The Analytics Services
1.text: Now the analytics services. Think of four stages, shown in the figure. Collect: Amazon Kinesis takes in streaming data, and Amazon S three holds the data lake. Prepare: A W S Glue discovers, catalogs and transforms the data. Analyze: Athena, Redshift, E M R and OpenSearch Service each answer different kinds of questions. And visualize: Amazon Quick builds dashboards. Amazon Quick evolved from Amazon QuickSight, which lives on as Amazon Quick Sight, so older material may use the earlier name. Exam tip: think collect, prepare, analyze, visualize, and then pick the service for each stage.

1.title: Streaming and Preparing Data: Kinesis, Firehose and AWS Glue
1.text: Three services handle streaming and preparing data. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams collects and processes large streams of data records in real time, and many applications can read one stream. Think real-time streams. Amazon Data Firehose delivers streaming data to S three, Redshift, OpenSearch Service and more, with no applications to write. It was earlier called Kinesis Data Firehose. Think of loading streams into stores. A W S Glue is serverless data integration. It discovers, prepares, moves and integrates data, with a Data Catalog, crawlers and E T L jobs, where E T L means extract, transform and load, and you pay as you go. Kinesis also includes Video Streams and Managed Service for Apache Flink. Exam tip: a live stream means Kinesis; delivering a stream to S three or Redshift means Firehose; catalog and E T L mean Glue.

1.title: Querying and Big Data: Athena, Redshift, EMR and OpenSearch
1.text: Four services answer questions about your data. Amazon Athena is a serverless service that runs interactive queries on data in Amazon S three, using standard S Q L. You pay for the queries you run. Think S Q L on S three files. Amazon Redshift is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse, and it has a Serverless option. Think data warehouse. Amazon E M R is a managed cluster platform for big data processing with Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark. Think big data frameworks. And Amazon OpenSearch Service is managed OpenSearch clusters for search, log analytics, application monitoring and clickstream analysis. Exam tip: S Q L on S three with no servers means Athena; a data warehouse means Redshift; search and logs mean OpenSearch.

1.title: What the Exam Asks: AI/ML and Analytics
1.text: Here is how the exam frames this module. Text, speech, image, document or chat: Comprehend and Translate, Transcribe and Polly, Rekognition and Textract, and Lex. Your own model: SageMaker A I. Streaming data: Kinesis Data Streams, or Firehose to deliver it. Prepare and catalog: A W S Glue. Query S three with S Q L: Athena. A warehouse: Redshift. Hadoop and Spark: E M R. Search and logs: OpenSearch. And dashboards: Amazon Quick. Exam tip: name the input or the stage, then the service.

1.title: Design Check: Tidewater's Data and AI Plan
1.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Sentiment in thousands of reviews: Amazon Comprehend. Text from scanned supplier invoices: Amazon Textract. Support call recordings turned into text: Amazon Transcribe. Product photos checked for unsafe content: Amazon Rekognition. A chatbot for order questions: Amazon Lex. Train its own forecasting model: Amazon SageMaker A I. Quick S Q L answers from sales files in S three: Amazon Athena. Website clicks as a live stream: Amazon Kinesis. Cleaning and cataloging the data: A W S Glue. And dashboards for managers: Amazon Quick. Pause the video if you want more time.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. The A I services, Comprehend, Translate, Transcribe, Polly, Rekognition, Textract and Lex, each do one task through an A P I. For your own models, use SageMaker A I. Bedrock offers foundation models, and Amazon Q is an A I assistant. For analytics, Kinesis handles streams, Firehose delivers them, and Glue prepares and catalogs the data. Athena runs S Q L on S three, Redshift is a warehouse, E M R runs Hadoop and Spark, and OpenSearch handles search and logs. And Amazon Quick, which evolved from QuickSight, shows the results.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Tidewater wants to find out whether thousands of customer reviews are positive, neutral or negative. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, Amazon Comprehend. It uses natural language processing to find sentiment, entities, key phrases and more in text. Textract reads scanned documents, Polly produces speech from text, and Transcribe turns audio into text.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which A W S service lets data scientists and developers build, train and deploy their own machine learning models? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, Amazon SageMaker A I, a fully managed machine learning service. Lex, Rekognition and Translate are pre-built A I services that each perform a specific task.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Tidewater wants a chatbot on its website that understands what customers ask, by voice or text, and answers order questions. Which service should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, Amazon Lex. It builds voice and text chatbots with speech recognition and natural language understanding. Polly only speaks text, Translate converts languages, and Textract extracts data from documents.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. The data team keeps sales files in Amazon S three and wants to run standard S Q L queries on them directly, without managing servers. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, Amazon Athena. It is a serverless service that runs standard S Q L directly on data in S three, and you pay for the queries you run. Redshift is a data warehouse, E M R runs big data frameworks on clusters, and OpenSearch Service handles search and logs.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Select two. Which two statements about analytics services are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and C. Kinesis Data Streams handles real-time streams, and Amazon Quick, which evolved from QuickSight, builds dashboards. Glue is a data integration service, Athena is serverless, and Polly turns text into speech rather than speech into text.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: A. Question two: C. Question three: B. Question four: D. Question five: B and C. That completes Module eleven. Next, Module twelve covers the remaining service categories: application integration, developer tools, end-user computing and more.
